items.title: Natural History of an Unusual Chorioretinal Phenotype Associated With the RHO p.(Met216Lys) Variant
items.abstract: Purpose: While variants in RHO are a leading cause of autosomal dominant retinitis pigmentosa (RP), the c.647T>A p.(Met216Lys) variant gives rise to a phenotype that can mimic choroideremia. We describe its long-term natural history. Methods: Patients were included from four centers (in France, the United Kingdom, and the United States). Clinical features analyzed included pedigrees, best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA), visual fields, color vision, electroretinography, and multimodal imaging (color fundus photography, short-wavelength and near-infrared fundus autofluorescence [SW- and NIR-AF], and spectral domain optical coherence tomography [SD-OCT]). Results: Seventeen patients (11 women; median age at first examination, 45 years [range, 13-68 years]) from eight unrelated families were included. Follow-up was available for 13 individuals (median, 159 months [range, 24-286 months]). Impaired night vision was the predominant presenting symptom (71%), with BCVA relatively preserved at baseline. Visual fields showed pericentral round scotomas, enlarging and coalescing over time, with relative sparing of the far periphery. On SW-AF, younger patients showed a diffuse granular pattern, whereas older patients showed well-demarcated patches of autofluorescence loss. Serial imaging in seven patients confirmed that these patches enlarged and coalesced within individuals over time. Color fundus photography showed preserved optic disc color and normal retinal vessel caliber. SD-OCT demonstrated outer retinal tubulations, a thinned choroid, and progressive ellipsoid zone (EZ) loss (median rate of EZ width loss, 176 µm per year). Conclusions: The RHO c.647T>A p.(Met216Lys) variant is associated with a slowly progressive, unusual chorioretinal dystrophy phenotype that can closely mimic choroideremia. Our findings suggest pathogenetic mechanisms that differ from typical RHO-associated RP.

items.title: Phenotypic Variability in Individuals With Genotype-Matched EYS - and USH2A -Associated Autosomal-Recessive Retinitis Pigmentosa
items.abstract: Purpose: Variable expressivity is well recognized in autosomal-dominant inherited retinal diseases (IRDs) but is increasingly observed and less well defined in recessive IRDs. Despite the traditional view of recessive IRDs as monogenic disorders with high penetrance, phenotypic differences among individuals sharing identical biallelic variants suggest additional disease modifiers. We quantified genotype-phenotype concordance in EYS- and USH2A-associated retinitis pigmentosa (RP) and characterized phenotypic variability among individuals with identical primary genotypes. Methods: Participants underwent standardized ophthalmic assessment with multimodal imaging. Longitudinal ellipsoid zone (EZ) widths were measured from optical coherence tomography (OCT) scans obtained ≥12 months apart. Baseline EZ width and age at OCT assessment were compared among individuals sharing identical primary genotypes. Genotype-matched comparisons in which younger individuals demonstrated smaller EZ widths than older counterparts were classified as age-discordant structural comparisons. Results: Ninety patients (41 EYS, 49 USH2A) were included. Recurrent variants EYS c.6416G>A (p.Cys2139Tyr) and USH2A c.2802T>G (p.Cys934Trp) were identified in 46% and 35% of probands, respectively. Females showed greater baseline EZ preservation, although differences were not statistically significant. Marked variability was observed within matched genotypes. Several genotype-matched comparisons demonstrated age-discordant structural variability, including younger individuals with substantially smaller EZ widths than older genotype-matched counterparts. In EYS-associated disease, the largest discordant comparison demonstrated 85.4% less EZ preservation in the younger individuals despite younger age, and the corresponding value in USH2A-associated disease was 81.8%. Intrafamilial discordance further supported the possibility of modifying influences beyond the primary genotype. Conclusions: Disease severity varied substantially among individuals sharing identical primary genotypes, supporting contributions from additional genetic or environmental modifiers. Translational Relevance: Recognition of variability within recessive IRDs has implications for prognosis, trial stratification, and interpretation of treatment response beyond genotype alone.

items.title: Tear Ferning Test in Sheep: Scale‐Based Analysis, STEPanizer Method, and Correlation With Conjunctival Histological Findings
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Objective To evaluate the precorneal tear film (PTF) of clinically healthy sheep using the tear ferning test (TFT) and investigate its association with conjunctival histological parameters. Animals Studied One hundred and thirty‐four eyes from 67 adult sheep. Procedures Tear samples were collected and graded by three evaluators using the Rolando and Masmali grading scales. Digital stereological analysis of tear ferning patterns was performed using STEPanizer to quantify crystalline points. Conjunctival histology included assessment of inflammatory cell infiltration and goblet cell (GC) density. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, Spearman's correlation, Kendall's coefficient of concordance, and simple linear regression. Results Rolando and Masmali grading scales showed strong positive correlations between right and left eyes ( r = 0.922 and 0.886, respectively; p < 0.0001), demonstrating high consistency between eyes. STEPanizer crystal point counts were strongly and negatively correlated with TFT grades on both scales ( r = −0.826 to −0.890; p < 0.0001). Linear regression showed that stereological measurements explained 66%–83% of the variation in TFT grades ( R 2 = 0.66–0.83). Interobserver agreement was acceptable (Kendall's W = 0.69; p < 0.05). No significant correlations were found between TFT grades and histological parameters. Mild lymphocytic infiltration predominated (83.96%), while only weak negative associations were observed between TFT grades, GC density, and inflammatory infiltrate. Conclusions In clinically healthy sheep, TFT patterns appear to be influenced primarily by tear film physicochemical characteristics rather than routine conjunctival histological findings. Combining TFT with digital stereological analysis provides an objective and feasible approach for PTF characterization in veterinary ophthalmology.
